The chart includes a legend on the right side, identifying each country by its corresponding line color. Grid lines are present to assist in reading the values more accurately. import pandas as pd
print(Path("summary.txt").read_text())
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv")
print(table.to_string(index=False))
source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
source = source.replace("Annual Population Growth Rates by Region (1980-2000)",
                        "Annual GDP Growth Rates by Country (1971-1990)")
source = source.replace("plt.ylabel('Population (Millions)', fontsize=12)",
                        "plt.ylabel('GDP Growth (%)', fontsize=12)")
source = source.replace("plt.gca().set_ylim(-1.35, 16.25)",
                        "plt.gca().set_ylim(-1.35, 22)")
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
ax = plt.gca()
print("\nTitle:", ax.get_title())
print("Y label:", ax.get_ylabel())
print("Y limits:", ax.get_ylim())
print("Legend:", ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1])
print("Table columns:", table.columns.tolist())
for line in ax.lines:
    rows = table[table['Country'] == line.get_label()]
    assert list(line.get_xdata()) == rows['Year'].tolist()
    assert list(line.get_ydata()) == rows['GDP Growth (%)'].tolist()
print("Verified: all plotted years and GDP growth values match table.csv.")
